blocks.text: HANGS Construction Services LLC. Invented procedures for a software demonstration.

Each Monday, roll the forecast forward thirteen weeks, Monday to Sunday, from the operating account's adjusted book balance in the latest bank reconciliation. Show receipts and disbursements by category for each week and the ending cash of each week.

Forecast a contract payment only when the construction contract is signed, at the net amount from the funds control estimate or the billing schedule, on the expected funds date. A letter of intent or a pipeline entry is listed but left out of the forecast. Every receipt is expected, not cash, until the bank shows it.

Forecast each open bill in the weekly run on or before its due date (PAY-1), a bill in the prepared batch at the batch amount, and a held bill in the run after its expected release at the amount expected to be paid. Leave out a duplicate, a bill already paid and a bill another HANGS entity pays.
CF-4 Committed Costs and Large Payments

Forecast committed construction costs from the project manager's billing forecast, each in the run on or before its due date. For any payment over $100,000.00, take the due date from the signed contract or purchase order; when the billing forecast gives another date, use the earlier date and report the conflict to the Controller.
CF-5 Debt Service and Recurring Payments

Forecast loan interest and principal from the loan terms on the actual days, rent and insurance from the prepaid schedule behind the recurring entries, and payroll from the payroll calendar at the latest approved funding.

Compare each week's ending cash with the minimum of PAY-8. For a week below it, show what would restore it: a discretionary payment that can be delayed, or a draw on the construction line within its availability. A person chooses.

Project Unrestricted Cash at each month-end against the lender's minimum liquidity covenant. Compare the forecast with last week's: the week just ended against what the bank shows, and each later week, with the reason for every change over $10,000.00.
The Controller reviews the forecast, its assumptions and its flags. Nothing is paid, posted or drawn because of the forecast; each payment, entry and draw keeps its own approval.

blocks.text: HANGS Construction Services LLC. Invented procedures for a software demonstration.

Vendor payments are released once a week, on Thursday, from the operating account. Each run pays the approved bills that fall due before the next run, so no bill is paid late and none is paid early without a reason.
A bill on hold or in dispute is not paid until the hold is released in writing. A bill addressed to another HANGS entity is paid by that entity only.

Keep at least $250,000.00 in the operating account after committed payroll. Expected receipts are not cash. The Controller and the CFO approve each run over $100,000.00 before release; the batch is prepared for them and never released by its preparer.

passages.q: Must HANGS Construction Services file Form 940 for 2026?
passages.a: You're subject to FUTA tax in 2026 on the wages you pay employees who aren't farmworkers or household workers if: you paid wages of $1,500 or more in any calendar quarter in 2025 or 2026, or you had one or more employees for at least some part of a day in any 20 or more different weeks in 2025 or 20 or more different weeks in 2026.

passages.q: What are the 2026 FUTA rate, wage base and credit?
passages.a: For 2026, the FUTA tax rate is 6.0%. The tax applies to the first $7,000 you pay to each employee as wages during the year. ... The credit may be as much as 5.4% of FUTA taxable wages. If you're entitled to the maximum 5.4% credit, the FUTA tax rate after credit is 0.6%.

passages.q: Do employees' 401(k) deferrals come off FUTA wages?
passages.a: Elective employee contributions and deferrals to a plan containing a qualified cash or deferred compensation arrangement (401(k)). Generally exempt, but see section 402(g) for limitation. Taxable. Taxable.

passages.q: When is the Q3 2026 Form 941 due?
passages.a: Your Form 941 is due by the last day of the month that follows the end of the quarter. ... 3. July, August, September September 30 October 31 ... If you made timely deposits in full payment of your taxes for the quarter, you may file by the 10th day of the 2nd month that follows the end of the quarter. ... If any due date for filing falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, you may file your return on the next business day.

passages.q: Which employees are counted on line 1, and what goes on lines 2 and 3?
passages.a: Enter the number of employees on your payroll for the pay period including March 12, June 12, September 12, or December 12, for the quarter indicated at the top of Form 941. ... Enter amounts on line 2 that would also be included in box 1 of your employees’ Forms W-2. ... Enter the federal income tax you withheld (or were required to withhold) from your employees on this quarter’s wages, tips, taxable fringe benefits, and supplemental unemployment compensation benefits.

passages.q: Which wages go on line 5a, and where does Social Security stop for each employee?
passages.a: The social security tax rate is 6.2% each for the employee and employer. The social security wage base limit is $184,500. ... For 2026, the rate of social security tax on taxable wages is 6.2% (0.062) each for the employer and employee. Stop paying social security tax on and entering an employee’s wages on line 5a when the employee’s taxable wages and tips reach $184,500 for the year. ... line 5a (column 1) x 0.124 line 5a (column 2)

sources.title: General Instructions for Forms W-2 and W-3 (2026)

passages.q: When are the 2026 Forms W-2 and W-3 due, and must they be e-filed?
passages.a: The due date for filing 2026 Forms W-2 ... and W-3 ... with the SSA is February 1, 2027, whether you file using paper forms or electronically. ... Generally, you must furnish Copies B, C, and 2 of Form W-2 to your employees by February 1, 2027. ... You must e-file Forms W-2 ... if you are required to file at least 10 information returns.

passages.q: What goes in box 1, and are the 401(k) deferrals and Washington Paid Leave premiums in it?
passages.a: Box 1-Wages, tips, other compensation. Show the total taxable wages, tips, and other compensation that you paid to your employee during the year. However, do not include elective deferrals (such as employee contributions to a section 401(k) or 403(b) plan) ... You must include the employee contribution and the employer voluntary payment as wages on the Form W-2.

passages.q: What are the 2026 Social Security limits for boxes 3 and 4, and what goes in boxes 5 and 6?
passages.a: The total of boxes 3 and 7 cannot exceed $184,500 (2026 maximum social security wage base). ... For 2026, the amount should not exceed $11,439 ... there is no wage base limit for Medicare tax ... an employer is required to withhold a 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax on any Federal Insurance Contributions Act (FICA) wages ... in excess of $200,000 in a calendar year.

policies.title: The Thirteen-Week Forecast
policies.text: Each Monday, roll the forecast forward thirteen weeks, Monday to Sunday, from the operating account's adjusted book balance in the latest bank reconciliation. Show receipts and disbursements by category for each week and the ending cash of each week.

policies.title: Receipts
policies.text: Forecast a contract payment only when the construction contract is signed, at the net amount from the funds control estimate or the billing schedule, on the expected funds date. A letter of intent or a pipeline entry is listed but left out of the forecast. Every receipt is expected, not cash, until the bank shows it.

policies.title: Payables
policies.text: Forecast each open bill in the weekly run on or before its due date (PAY-1), a bill in the prepared batch at the batch amount, and a held bill in the run after its expected release at the amount expected to be paid. Leave out a duplicate, a bill already paid and a bill another HANGS entity pays.

policies.title: Committed Costs and Large Payments
policies.text: Forecast committed construction costs from the project manager's billing forecast, each in the run on or before its due date. For any payment over $100,000.00, take the due date from the signed contract or purchase order; when the billing forecast gives another date, use the earlier date and report the conflict to the Controller.

policies.title: Debt Service and Recurring Payments
policies.text: Forecast loan interest and principal from the loan terms on the actual days, rent and insurance from the prepaid schedule behind the recurring entries, and payroll from the payroll calendar at the latest approved funding.

policies.title: Minimum Balance
policies.text: Compare each week's ending cash with the minimum of PAY-8. For a week below it, show what would restore it: a discretionary payment that can be delayed, or a draw on the construction line within its availability. A person chooses.

policies.title: Covenants and Variances
policies.text: Project Unrestricted Cash at each month-end against the lender's minimum liquidity covenant. Compare the forecast with last week's: the week just ended against what the bank shows, and each later week, with the reason for every change over $10,000.00.

policies.title: Approval
policies.text: The Controller reviews the forecast, its assumptions and its flags. Nothing is paid, posted or drawn because of the forecast; each payment, entry and draw keeps its own approval.

policies.title: Weekly Payment Run
policies.text: Vendor payments are released once a week, on Thursday, from the operating account. Each run pays the approved bills that fall due before the next run, so no bill is paid late and none is paid early without a reason.

policies.title: Holds and Disputes
policies.text: A bill on hold or in dispute is not paid until the hold is released in writing. A bill addressed to another HANGS entity is paid by that entity only.

policies.title: Cash and Approval
policies.text: Keep at least $250,000.00 in the operating account after committed payroll. Expected receipts are not cash. The Controller and the CFO approve each run over $100,000.00 before release; the batch is prepared for them and never released by its preparer.

checks.title: Below the Minimum Balance · PAY-8, CF-6
checks.detail: Week 6 ends at $209,598.57, $40,401.43 below the $250,000.00 minimum of PAY-8. Week 6 has $734,600.00 going out and nothing coming in: PO-27-0511 Ironvale Steel Buildings $552,000.00 on December 8; Compact track loader to replace the storm-repair rental, Kestrel Ridge Equipment Quote KRE-Q-2290 $94,800.00 on December 10; SC-27-05-01 Bluepine Concrete Works $46,200.00 on December 10. The next receipts are Draw 9, Site 19 in week 7. Under CF-6 a person chooses what restores it. Option A: delay the compact track loader to replace the storm-repair rental, $94,800.00 planned December 10, which is discretionary and has no purchase order; week 6 would end at $304,398.57. Option B: draw on the construction line, at least $40,401.43 before December 8, within the $142,912.00 still available under the $5,000,000.00 commitment after Draws 8 to 10. Nothing is delayed or drawn by this forecast.

checks.title: Payment Date Conflict · CF-4, PAY-1
checks.detail: The $552,000.00 steel balance on PO-27-0511 is due on delivery, December 8, by the signed order; the billing forecast says January 7. The project manager's billing forecast puts the balance owed to Ironvale Steel Buildings at an invoice on delivery with the vendor file's net 30 terms, so it would be paid in the January 7 run. The signed purchase order says: "Balance of $552,000.00 due on delivery, by wire, before the packages are unloaded." Under CF-4 a payment over $100,000.00 takes its date from the signed contract, and the earlier date is used, so the forecast pays it by wire on December 8, in week 6. That is what takes week 6 below the minimum. If the vendor agrees to net 30, the payment moves to week 10; the Controller confirms the terms with Ironvale Steel Buildings and the project manager corrects one of the two.

checks.title: Expected Receipt Without a Signed Contract · CF-2, PAY-8
checks.detail: Site 27 is on the billing schedule for December 23 at $447,265.00 of net payment, with no signed construction contract. Business development lists Harborline Storage Co. for Site 27 at $455,000.00: "Letter of intent signed October 28; construction contract in negotiation; no customer deposit" Under CF-2 a contract payment is forecast only when the construction contract is signed; a letter of intent is listed but left out, and PAY-8 says expected receipts are not cash. The forecast leaves out the $447,265.00; last week's forecast counted it in the week of December 21. If the contract is signed and the customer's deposit is received, it can come in next Monday's forecast.

checks.title: Planned Draws Assumed · CF-2, CF-7
checks.detail: Draw 9 and Draw 10, $764,288.00, are in the forecast but not yet submitted to Harrow Point Lending. Draw 9 is $174,368.00, 80% of $217,960.00 of financed hard costs billed in November, funding December 16; Draw 10 is $589,920.00, 80% of $737,400.00 of financed hard costs billed in December, funding January 15. Draw 8 is approved at $252,800.00. The planned draws assume the lender inspects and funds the full advance on time; they are expected receipts, not cash. Without them, Unrestricted Cash at January 31 would be $720,957.39, below the $750,000.00 of Section 7.3, and $892,311.32 at December 31. The Controller confirms the amounts and dates with the lender before the forecast is relied on.

checks.title: Controller Review of the Forecast · CF-8
checks.detail: The Controller reviews the forecast, its assumptions and its flags. Nothing is paid, posted or drawn because of it.

checks.title: Start from the October bank reconciliation's adjusted book balance
checks.detail: Cash starts at $1,029,176.48: GL 1010's $1,029,106.01 with the bank's interest credit, less its service charge, the wire fee and check 10431 recorded short, the reconciliation's proposed entries (CF-1). The minimum the payment procedures keep is $250,000.00 after committed payroll (PAY-8); runs are on Thursdays (PAY-1).

checks.title: Compare last week's forecast for the week ended November 1 with the bank
checks.detail: Last week's forecast ended the week at $1,305,589.44; the bank ended it at $1,029,176.48, $276,412.96 lower. Site 22's $437,500.00 did not come in: the milestone billing moved to November 6. The customer's $25,000.00 deposit came instead, and the October 29 run was held for the close, so $136,003.00 of bills move into the November 5 batch. The opening differs by -$57.00, the reconciliation's two corrections.

checks.title: Put the prepared November 5 batch in at its net
checks.detail: The payment run's batch pays 11 bills in 7 payments for $136,003.00 after $592.00 of early-pay discounts. It waits for the Controller and the CFO (PAY-8); the forecast assumes its release on November 5. Payroll of $97,318.40 is approved and funds November 6.

checks.title: Schedule every other open bill in its Thursday run
checks.detail: Of the aging's $350,734.56, 11 open bills are paid in the run on or before their due dates and 3 held bills in the run after their expected release (CF-3, PAY-7): KRE-2207 $76,167.00 on November 19; MLE-1401 $8,800.00 on November 12; SWR-8133 $14,300.00 on November 19. A duplicate, a bill already paid and another entity's bill, $18,502.00, are left out.

checks.title: Fund payroll on the calendar's dates
checks.detail: Seven payrolls fund in the thirteen weeks, November 6 to January 29, the December 31 one early for the January 1 holiday. November 6 is the approved preview; the rest are at that latest approved funding (CF-5), $681,228.80 in all.

checks.title: Tie Site 22 to the funds control payment estimate
checks.detail: Site 22 bills November 6 and funds control wires $412,500.00 on November 10: the $445,000.00 milestone billing less the $25,000.00 customer deposit already received and $7,500.00 of owner deductions. The billing schedule agrees to the cent.

checks.title: Count only payments under a signed construction contract
checks.detail: 5 sites have signed contracts, $1,958,005.00 of expected net payments. Site 27 is on the billing schedule for December 23 at $447,265.00 of net payment, with no signed construction contract. It is left out (CF-2).

checks.title: Schedule the construction draws
checks.detail: Draw 8 is approved at $252,800.00 and funds November 9. Draws 9 and 10 are planned at the 80% advance rate on financed Larkfield hard costs billed in November and December: $174,368.00 and $589,920.00. After them, $142,912.00 is left under the $5,000,000.00 commitment.

checks.title: Take PO-27-0511's due date from the signed order
checks.detail: The $552,000.00 steel balance on PO-27-0511 is due on delivery, December 8, by the signed order; the billing forecast says January 7. The forecast uses December 8, the earlier date (CF-4).

checks.title: Schedule the committed construction costs
checks.detail: The project manager's billing forecast has 39 bills for $1,344,787.50; $1,246,487.50 falls due in the thirteen weeks, each in the run on or before its due date. Financed Larkfield hard costs are $217,960.00 billed in November and $737,400.00 in December; Granite Point Business Park is paid from operating cash.

checks.title: Work out loan interest and principal on the actual days
checks.detail: Construction loan interest at 6.25% on the daily balance: October $19,808.22, paid November 16 because the 15th is a Sunday; November $20,678.35 with Draw 8; December $22,203.20 with Draw 9. The equipment loan pays $4,313.17 of interest for October to December, October's from the close's schedule, and its first $15,500.00 principal installment on December 31.

checks.title: Carry rent, insurance and the monthly items from the close's schedules
checks.detail: Rent is paid quarterly in advance: RJ-02's $9,600.00 a month makes $28,800.00 for January to March, paid December 29, 3 days ahead as last quarter. RJ-01 insurance is amortization of premiums already paid; neither policy renews before April 1, so no premium falls in the thirteen weeks. Utilities and the service charge repeat October's.

checks.title: Roll the thirteen weeks forward
checks.detail: From $1,029,176.48, $2,975,093.00 of expected receipts and $2,519,524.09 of disbursements end week 13, January 31, 2027, at $1,484,745.39. The lowest week is week 6, the week of December 7, at $209,598.57.

checks.title: Test every week against the $250,000.00 minimum
checks.detail: Week 6 ends at $209,598.57, $40,401.43 below the $250,000.00 minimum of PAY-8. Option A, delay the discretionary loader: week 6 ends at $304,398.57. Option B, draw at least $40,401.43 on the construction line, within $142,912.00 available. A person chooses (CF-6).

checks.title: Project Unrestricted Cash at each month-end against Section 7.3
checks.detail: Unrestricted Cash, the operating account plus petty cash, meets the lender's $750,000.00 at November 30, December 31 and January 31; the least headroom is $316,679.32 at December 31. Without the planned Draws 9 and 10, January 31 would be $720,957.39, below it. Sections 7.1 and 7.2 are tested in the monthly reporting package.

checks.title: Compare this forecast with last week's, week by week
checks.detail: Week 12 ends at $1,250,677.72 against last week's $1,703,427.08. The week ended November 1 came in $276,412.96 lower, and the twelve weeks changed by -$176,336.40: Site 22 moved in and Site 27 out, the held bills moved, Draw 8 came in lower. The steel balance moved from week 10 to week 6 (CF-7).

checks.title: Add up the flags for the Controller
checks.detail: Ending cash $1,484,745.39; lowest week 6 at $209,598.57. 4 flags: the week below the minimum, the steel payment's date, Site 27 without a contract and the planned draws. Nothing was paid, posted or drawn.
